# Set-ZbxUserGroup

## SYNOPSIS

Changes a user group.

## SYNTAX

```
Set-ZbxUserGroup [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixUserGroup>[]> [[-Name] <string>] [-DebugMode <bool>] [-GuiAccess <ZabbixGuiAccess>] [-UsersStatus <ZabbixGroupStatus>] [-UserDirectoryId <ulong>] [-MfaStatus <bool>] [-MfaId <ulong>] [-Right <ZabbixUserGroupRightRequest[]>] [-HostGroupRight <ZabbixUserGroupHostGroupRightRequest[]>] [-TemplateGroupRight <ZabbixUserGroupTemplateGroupRightRequest[]>] [-TagFilter <ZabbixUserGroupTagFilterRequest[]>] [-User <ZabbixReference<ZabbixUser>[]>] [-Proxy <ZabbixReference<ZabbixProxy>[]>] [-ProxyGroup <ZabbixReference<ZabbixProxyGroup>[]>] [-ProxyMode <ZabbixProxyMode>] [-ProxyGroupMode <ZabbixProxyGroupMode>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-PassThru] [-PipedRecord <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A user group is a named set of users that sets their permissions on host and template groups, their frontend access and their authentication. The Set-ZbxUserGroup cmdlet changes the user groups given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped objects) with usergroup.update; a field whose parameter is not given keeps its value. Every user group the pipeline brings is changed in one call when the pipeline ends, and -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name. The command writes nothing unless -PassThru is given, which reads the changed user groups back and writes them; -WhatIf shows what would change.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Change a user group

```powershell
Set-ZbxUserGroup -InputObject 'Night shift' -GuiAccess Disabled
```

Keeps the members of the user group Night shift out of the frontend; the API still accepts them.

### Example 2: Change a user group and write the result

```powershell
Set-ZbxUserGroup -InputObject 'Night shift' -GuiAccess Disabled -PassThru
```

The same change with -PassThru, which reads the user group Night shift back from the server and writes it; without it the command writes nothing.
